column1: Initialize a local Git repository at the chosen project or solution root with {{c1::git init}}.
column2:
git init creates local repository metadata at the chosen root. It does not add files to a commit or configure a remote. The team can then track schema files and deployment scripts together.
Review source

column1: Share repository-wide ignore patterns through a versioned {{c1::.gitignore}} file.
column2:
Version the ignore file so everyone uses the same rules for generated output. Ignore patterns affect untracked files. Adding a rule does not stop Git from tracking a file that it already tracks.
Review source

column1: Declare prep-db.sql as the pre-deployment entry script with {{c1::<PreDeploy Include="prep-db.sql" />}}.
column2:
PreDeploy identifies the one entry file for work that runs before the schema changes. Place it inside an ItemGroup in the project file. The deployment plan is already calculated when the script runs.
Review source

column1: Declare PostDeploy.sql as the post-deployment entry script with {{c1::<PostDeploy Include="PostDeploy.sql" />}}.
column2:
PostDeploy identifies the entry file that runs after planned schema changes. Use includes in that file to arrange smaller seed scripts in order, such as parent lookup rows before dependent rows.
Review source

column1: In a SQLCMD deployment script, read the seed file at this point with {{c1:::r}} .\Scripts\PostDeployment\seed-statuses.sql.
column2:
The SQLCMD :r directive reads another file at that point in the entry script. Include order matters if a later script needs lookup values inserted by an earlier one.
Review source

column1: Exclude seed.sql from SDK-style model compilation with {{c1::<Build Remove="seed.sql" />}}.
column2:
Build Remove keeps the seed file out of the compiled model. The file remains on disk and still becomes part of the deployment script if the entry file references it with :r.
Review source

column1: After excluding seed.sql from the compiled model, keep it visible in an SDK-style project with {{c1::<None Include="seed.sql" />}}.
column2:
The None item can keep the file visible in the project without compiling it into the schema model. Build Remove handles model exclusion. The SQLCMD include handles deployment packaging.
Review source

column1: For MERGE aliases target and source, match rows by StatusID with {{c1::ON target.StatusID = source.StatusID}}.
column2:
StatusID identifies the same status in both sets of rows. Match on that stable ID so a renamed StatusName updates the existing row instead of treating its new label as a new status.
Review source

column1: In a reference data MERGE, update existing matches with {{c1::WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET}} followed by assignments.
column2:
This branch runs for a source row whose key already exists in the target. For example, set target.StatusName to source.StatusName to rename the status without changing its ID.
Review source

column1: In a reference data MERGE, insert source rows missing from the target with {{c1::WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT}}.
column2:
This branch runs when a source key does not exist in the target. List the destination columns and their values for the insert. End the complete MERGE statement with a semicolon.
